then.text: Saturday at Bethania. I've written it on the bar. Mind, it's written under a pint.
Second tenor? Me? Aye, I sing. But I'll be damned if I give my voice for free. Answer this: who wrote 'Myfanwy', Merthyr's own?
Joseph Parry! Born a stone's throw from the bar. I'll sing. And I'll bring half the regulars, they'll sing too whether they like it or not.
You found a second tenor for the eisteddfod choir.

else.text: No, bach. Elgar's English. Think of the busker outside the pub: he's humming it. Come back when you know.
Y Dic Penderyn, the pub. Named for the Merthyr boy hanged in Cardiff in 1831. We don't have a statue in here, just a very big portrait and a very strong opinion.
I'm a second tenor on a good night. If there's ever a choir that needs one, ask.

mer_regular.text: Chwarae teg, that's fair play, and you've not had a drink so you're playing fair. I'll have yours.
There's a pub quiz on Thursdays. Tough one. The local history round has a question about every single ironmaster and a different one about what they did to their workers.
